_comment: Where tools/title_progress.py finds Call of Duty: Black Ops and what cannot be read from its sources. Paths are this machine's checkouts; nothing of the title is in this repository.
name: Call of Duty: Black Ops

sys.where: all eight groups, by default (`--any360_sys_groups=none` for ReXGlue's kernel); no call reaches ReXGlue's kernel, its local server's sockets on Any360's network (loopback: nothing leaves the machine); played 10 minutes in a level

gfx.where: by default (`--any360_gpu=false` for ReXGlue's GPU); menus, a campaign level and Zombies drawn through `any360::gfx` at 60 FPS, 10 minutes in a level with no GPU reset since the translator's forward jumps stay in one pass
todo: Models that flicker in the first seconds of a level (draws skipped while their pipelines compile in the background).
Short green artifacts at the start of a level, and lighting that shifts with the camera's rotation.
Dotted artifacts on some items (also on ReXGlue's Vulkan backend: the shared translator).

next: Play the campaign past its first level and Zombies past a few rounds on the default binding: saves, sound, the gamepad.
Find the XDK and C runtime functions Any360 already has (`memcpy`, `memset`, the string functions) in this executable and bind them after a check in game.
open: With only some system groups switched, the game can report a missing asset (`couldn't find shell shock 'flashbang'`) or stop drawing: each group alone needs the others' objects (events, APCs, completion ports), so those runs say little; the full binding is what counts.
